# Security verdict: pass-with-notes

PR #295 (F241), exact head ef7fda74f0eaec50f730abe4d28e4ad8b98f876f.
Answers security/295 request 01a1f9ae-55d0-7ff0-83e1-0f3af7a963e3.

No demonstrated exploitable security vulnerability was found in the 16 changed files under C33's user-account trust boundary. This verdict does not certify race-free deletion or an enforced private-directory precondition. No source changes, dependency installation, live sweep --apply, or holding release was performed.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | None demonstrated under C33 | - |

## Destructive policy and brake

The anchored, case-sensitive fixture prefixes in crates/testkit/src/tmux_sweep.rs:37-49,144-146 are pij-test-, pij-rs-, pij180-, pij-utf8-, and p139-boot-. They do not match default, pij, or work.

Deletion POLICY: fixture namespace; eligible uid-owned socket or regular, single-link lock; no answering server; for a lock, successful nonblocking flock with unlink while the File remains held. ConnectionRefused permits stale classification; successful connect preserves the entry. Other returned connect errors, including EACCES, ENOENT, and timeout, classify as Unsure and preserve it (186-190). No explicit connect timeout is configured.

The 600-second mtime test (174-178) is a one-directional BRAKE: young entries and missing/future timestamps are spared. Removing it permits the same deletions or more; age is not deletion authority and provides no race-safety guarantee.

Entry symlinks are excluded through symlink_metadata; sockets must be uid-owned (194-199), locks must be uid-owned regular files with one link (214-219), and lock open uses OPEN_NO_FOLLOW without create/truncate (231-234). Nonblocking flock and lock unlink occur at 238-243.

## Known limits and nonblocking follow-ups

1. Directory validation is not enforced. crates/testkit/src/tmux.rs:29-34 canonicalizes the base and appends tmux-<uid>; tmux_sweep.rs:125-157 does not verify the resulting directory's owner, mode, or symlink status. A read-only probe observed the default directory to be uid-owned, a real nonsymlink directory, and mode 0700. That observation is not an invariant. C33 does not exempt a hostile other-user-controlled directory; no cross-user exploit was demonstrated here. Making the private-directory precondition explicit is a follow-up.

2. Deletion is pathname-based (tmux_sweep.rs:157,243), without dirfd/unlinkat, post-open inode validation, or final path identity comparison. Holding a checked lock inode does not certify that its pathname still refers to that inode. Same-user hostile replacement is outside C33; ordinary fixture races remain the correctness reviewer's responsibility. This verdict does not repeat a blanket claim that lock-then-unlink is race-free against any same-name replacement.

3. The paired-socket metadata probe at tmux_sweep.rs:224 uses is_ok(), so all metadata errors are treated as absence and skip connect. The connect classifier itself fails closed, but this metadata branch does not distinguish ENOENT from permission or other failures. An otherwise eligible, old, unlocked lock can consequently be removed. No demonstrated exploitable security vulnerability was established; distinguishing genuine absence is a concrete follow-up.

4. Fixture cleanup runs after kill-server attempts, not after proof that every kill succeeded. PrivateTmux uses a PID, process-local atomic counter, and timestamp component (tmux.rs:83-92); Drop attempts kill-server then calls cleanup (146-150). remove_server_files unlinks the lock then socket directly (67-69), without liveness or flock checks. Other named fixtures follow the kill-then-cleanup order; governance_boot kills/reaps its owned foreground child before cleanup (crates/cli/tests/governance_boot.rs:212-218). No reviewed production cleanup route uses this helper. There is intentionally no product retention/unlink rule for opened F229 locks.

No C21 secret, private-content, or hardcoded machine-home-path finding was identified in the changed lines.

## Cost and harness feedback

No daemon timer, per-tick loop, or per-seat process launch is introduced. Fixture Drop adds filesystem unlink operations after the existing kill-server launch; the sweep is an explicit one-shot directory scan with in-process connect and locking, not an ambient poll.

Harness difficulty DL-001: read-only boot recommends worktree dependency links despite C25. Magic wand: a C25-aware review mode that reports exact-head CI evidence without recommending links or treating missing JS tools as repository defects. Captured through harness observe in the ignored per-agent buffer; no product or governance ledger was edited by hand.

The security/295 holding is retained until merge.
